Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE finished vertical 9:16 Instagram story creative, 1080x1920 composition, a stronger creative variation of the supplied Charlotte photography invitation.
Input image: reference for the actual three people, their photographic images, and DIY art direction. Preserve all three faces, hair, clothing and photo character closely. The curly-haired man holding the phone is the photographer and must be labeled "me", never represented as a customer transformation. The woman and wavy-haired man are portfolio portraits. Use only these photographic subjects; no invented people.
Concept 01: THE RED CONTACT SHEET. Confident, perfectly balanced refined version of the original: warm ivory full-page contact-sheet paper, huge red hand-brushed "Charlotte" across the upper 18%, black condensed uppercase "FREE PHOTO SHOOT" immediately beneath, easy to read on a phone. Below a tight 2x2 grid of black film borders with the photographer upper left, female portrait upper right, male portrait lower left, near-black empty lower right frame with huge red handwritten "you?". Red wax-pencil circles/annotations connect "me" to "you?". The grid fills the page decisively with only comfortable margins, not the enormous empty black lower area of the reference. Small black handwritten "DM me" centered at bottom. Authentic editorial photography invitation, tactile paper, subtle grain, darkroom amber frame counters, lively hand-drawn energy, excellent typographic hierarchy and no overlaps that obscure words or faces.
Exact visible words only: "Charlotte", "FREE PHOTO SHOOT", "me", "you?", "DM me". Small numeric film frame counters allowed.
No logos, watermarks, UI chrome, invented dates, fabricated promises, extra people, multi-design contact sheet, or additional copy.

Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE finished vertical 9:16 Instagram story image for a free Charlotte photo shoot. The attached reference is the source of the three photographic subjects and visual taste: red expressive handwritten marks, warm ivory paper, black film frames, tactile analog photography. Preserve the actual appearance and identity of all three people closely: curly-haired photographer holding phone in pink shirt and black bag, East Asian woman with long straight black hair and black top, young wavy-haired male in dark open-collar shirt. The selfie man is the photographer; label only him "me". The two other photos are portfolio examples. Do not invent replacement people, put different clothes on them, or present anyone as a before/after. Recompose and recrop those three photos freely while preserving their faces. Render lettering beautifully and correctly, with a hierarchy instantly readable on a phone. This is a graphic-design variation, not a photo of a poster in an environment. All important text and faces inside comfortable margins. Genuine grain and restrained paper texture. No logos, brand names, watermarks, UI chrome, invented dates, pricing, guaranteed results, or extra words. Output one design only, never a grid of multiple designs. Exact main offer words "Charlotte" and "FREE PHOTO SHOOT" must be clearly visible. Other allowed words only "me", "you?", "DM me". Tiny frame numerals permitted. Concept: PHOTO BOOTH INVITATION. Warm ivory field. Very large black condensed "CHARLOTTE" (uppercase rendering of Charlotte) near the top, "FREE PHOTO SHOOT" in red hand-lettered capitals beneath. A dramatically enlarged vertical black photo-booth strip crosses the center with three consecutive image windows: the two portfolio portraits and a dark last window containing huge red handwritten "you?". The strip is rotated just slightly, takes roughly 70% of the width and 62% of the height, and looks like a real continuous analog print. The photographer selfie appears in a smaller separate taped square print overlapping the strip edge at lower left with red "me" beneath it. A single sweeping red pencil arrow travels from me toward the empty window. Large handwritten "DM me" at the bottom. Fresh, playful, uncluttered, art-directed like an independent fashion magazine. Make every photo large enough to recognize.
